steps.text: Place spinach, water, bouillon, onion, and garlic powder in a large pot over medium-high heat; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer until onion is tender.

Meanwhile, melt butter in a small saucepan; whisk in flour until smooth and cook for 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in half-and-half until smooth; add to soup. Simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Creamy Spinach Soup
raw_recipe.description: This creamy spinach soup recipe is made with frozen spinach, onion, bouillon granules, garlic powder, and half-and-half. Serve it topped with croutons.
raw_recipe.name: Creamy Spinach Soup

recipeInstructions.text: Place spinach, water, bouillon, onion, and garlic powder in a large pot over medium-high heat; bring to a boil. Reduce heat to medium-low; simmer until onion is tender.

Meanwhile, melt butter in a small saucepan; whisk in flour until smooth and cook for 2 minutes. Slowly whisk in half-and-half until smooth; add to soup. Simmer until thickened, about 10 minutes. Season with salt and black pepper.

review.reviewBody: Great recipe! I did make changes in preparation beginning with sauteeing the onion & fresh garlic and then adding chicken broth instead of the water. I did not thaw the spinach but did puree the spinach/broth/onion mixture before adding the cream base. To cut fat I substituted 1 1/2 cups of half-and-half with a can of evaporated milk. We will definitely be making this a lot -- easy and very satisfying. Thanks for a great recipe.

I changed it a lot by sauteing the onion and garlic in olive oil 1st, 2nd add water and one grated potato(for thickener)Puree in a blender and return to pot. 3rd use 1% Milk instead of 1/2 and 1/2. This cuts the saturated fat and calories immensely and will help your healthy lifestyle. Enjoy and live long!

Very good soup! I made a few changes though. I sauteed the onion until soft and then added water and bullion. Then I added two large chopped potatoes and about 1/4 tsp of cayenne pepper. I skipped the flour part mostly because I didn't want to dirty more dishes (I have a 5 month old baby and no time). I used 1lb of fresh spinach and added it to the soup once potatoes were soft. After spinach was wilted I blended the whole thing with a hand blender until smooth. We ate it with grated parmesan cheese. Really great and so healthy!

I followed other reviewers and sauteed the garlic and onion, pureed the spinach mixture after boiling, and added cayenne pepper and celery salt for taste. With the extra additions, it was delicious and flavorful. In my husband's words, "better than expected."

I've always been a fan of creamed spinach but I wanted this to be more flavorful and thick. I minced fresh garlic and softened it with the sliced onions in a bit of olive oil with salt and then tossed in the chopped spinach. I melted butter, (didn't touch the flour), cream cheese, heavy whipping cream, a spot of milk, and added some nutmeg, and a couple other seasonings. Paired beautifully with a grilled cheese and I'll be making it again soon. I might try switching up my own variation just for kicks.

I made this soup, with a few changes, and it was fabulous! I'm strict low-carb, so I omitted the flour and used heavy cream instead. The cream thickened up the soup nicely. I also sauteed onions and fresh garlic in butter before adding the broth and spinach. Finally, I used fresh baby spinach instead of frozen. I didn't bother to chop it up or cook it ahead of time. I just tossed it with the broth and let it cook for 10-12 minutes or so, stirring occasionally. I also garnished with a sprinkle of shredded Parmesan. This is a keeper and I will be making it often!

Thank you for sharing this recipe! I only made a couple of minor changes to it. I used a teaspoon of chopped garlic instead of powder. Then I melted two tablespoons of butter in the pot, and sautéed both the onion and garlic before adding the spinach. I also used a can of chicken broth instead of chicken bouillon, and two cups of heavy cream instead of three cups of half and half. It came out good and thick the way I like it. This soup was easy to make and it was delicious!! My family devoured it!

Wow this was actually really good. I used fresh spinach and garlic (2) for the 5 servings. I didn't have half-n-half, so I used 2 cups of heavy cream and 1 cup of milk. I cooked the chopped onions and garlic for a bit before adding the spinach.

This soup ROCKED it! I used fresh spinach. I took the advice to salute the onion and garlic separately before cooking with the spinach. I used chicken broth in place of water. I pureed the spinach mixture once cooked, then added the milk mixture to it with about 1/4 sherry. I sauteed some fresh sliced mushrooms in butter and some sherry, then added to the soup in their sliced form. Be sure to salute the mushrooms for a really long time -- initially they release some water and there seems to be a lot of liquid with that and the sherry and butter, but keep going -- when the mushrooms caramelize, that is when you add them to the soup. It was DIVINE. Great recipe!

My husband said it was perfect the way it was but I think it was little rich. I deviated from the recipe as follows: I sauteed 1 cup of onion with about 3 large cloves of garlic in olive oil then added the frozen spinach, water, and a few chicken bullion cubes. After that cooked for a while I added the entire carton of half n half which was 4 cups, and some pepper. I melted some butter and added flour to it and whisked, then added it to the rest of the soup. Brought that to a boil and served a few minutes later. Oh and I added about 1 more cup of water to make up for the extra cream. Pretty good! I want to try fresh spinach next time. I also think it might be good with some diced tomatoes.

Very good! Personal preference I used about 2T of sour cream instead of 1/2&1/2 and a single serving container of Chobani vanilla & cinnamon Greek yogurt. And a bit of Mrs. Dash for added flavor. I also added a sweet potato. Puréed all after cooking, so yummy!
Great recipe! Would love to try with broccoli or cauliflower. This was a big hit with the fam. Will probably sauté the onions first next time tho.
I added gnocchi to ours but followed the soup recipe as is. Loved it!
Simple, basic creamy spinach soup you can improvise on. Sauteing the onions would have made them less sharp, still very good. The entire large stock pot of soup disappeared in one dinner.
So, if I want to can this spinach soup, how long should I pressure can this in pint jars?
Easy to make. Closest to Stouffer's Cream of Spinach, 35 years ago! Will use base for broccoli, cauliflower and whatever I feel.

I made this exactly as written and it turned out perfectly! As a few other reviewers said, it might be fun to try minced garlic along with the onion (in place of some of the garlic powder), but this recipe is fabulous as is.

Everyone loved it, and we'll definitely be making again. I did have a few changes: Fresh baby Spinach (maybe 1/3 lb) not frozen, a full onion, Minced garlic not powder, and I added 2 Minced carrots. We didn't have half and half. So I did half a cup heavy cream and 2.5c milk.
